To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cognitive model that was created based on ACT-R architecture provided a better fit to the learning and task performance data than the model that was based on the ACT model, and that the cognitive model provided good predictions of learning and task performance.

the cognitive model that learns from both the upfront instructional material and OTS instructions provides good fits to the data collected from human trainees, and that it is critical to closely monitor the training process of the trainees in order to provide instructional interventions that are effective at different stages of learning.
OTS instruction facilitates short-term learning, but its effects diminish when the OTS instruction is proceduralized in later training stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cognitive model-based training system for real-time instructional support.
the development of intelligent training systems that can provide adaptive instructions to trainees based on their learning processes.
the development of a training system that provides real-time instructional materials to trainees as needed, based on their actions and learning processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this research suggest that the use of real-time instructional interventions in a model-based training system can be an effective means to improve learning.
the results of this research are encouraging and provide the foundation for the development of a new generation of intelligent training systems.

a real-time training system based on a cognitive model that monitors learning and provides real-time instructional interventions at different stages of learning can be a viable solution to the problem of providing effective training to the military.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a model-based training system can be used to support the learning process of human learners, and that the model itself can be used to guide the development of such systems.

we developed a real-time modelbased training system that provides OTS instructions to trainees, and that we demonstrated that the OTS instructions can improve the learning and performance of human trainees.
the ACT-R architecture provides a solid theoretical foundation for the development of such an adaptive model-based training system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cognitive model can be used to predict learning, and this prediction can be used to provide real-time instructional support to the trainee.

a real-time model of learning and performance can be used as the foundation of an intelligent training system that can provide adaptive OTS instructions to trainees at different stages of their learning.
a cognitive model can be used as a learning and performance monitor to support adaptive training.
